verdict.rationale: None of the evidence documents self-managed deployment, a private or dedicated instance, or running Supabase Auth against your own database. The GitHub repo snippets describe configuration options (signup toggles, password rules, refresh-token rotation) but never state the server can be self-hosted. 'Standalone product' and 'connect this data to your own tables' describe how the product is used and how its data links to your tables, not where it runs.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can control where the auth system and its user data run — self-managed deployment, private instance, or my own database
